transcript.content: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.
Source offer offer-4a04f238-7424-498f-bd1d-0b684e38a2de: How should the user-selected fill be applied and what is the default when no fill is given?

sourceOffers.scope: The smallest change to the existing renderer: `render` gains an optional fill parameter that (a) leaves the current single-argument output byte-identical when fill is not supplied, and (b) emits a fill attribute when a fill is supplied. Nothing else changes: no rewrite of the label path, no new dependencies, no new API surface beyond the optional argument.
sourceOffers.question: How should the user-selected fill be applied and what is the default when no fill is given?

options.label: Optional fill argument; attribute omitted when absent
options.tradeoff: Most conservative delta: `render(label, fill?)` adds ` fill="..."` to the generated markup only when fill is provided, so existing single-argument callers and the existing test output stay literally unchanged. Costs: absent fill produces markup with no fill attribute, which inherits SVG defaults rather than having an explicit color — a caller wanting an explicit default must pass one.
options.acceptanceExample: render('A') === '<text>A</text>' (unchanged); render('A', 'red') === '<text fill="red">A</text>'; the existing test passes unmodified.

options.label: Optional fill argument with an explicit default in output
options.tradeoff: Same optional argument, but when no fill is supplied the software picks a declared default color and always emits ` fill="…"`. Costs: the current markup is no longer byte-identical for existing callers, so the existing test's expected value must keep matching either by keeping fill internal-only for the legacy path or by updating the expectation — and updating the expectation is a change to a working behavior that needs the operator's explicit choice of default color.
options.acceptanceExample: render('A', 'red') === '<text fill="red">A</text>'; render('A') === '<text fill="#000000">A</text>' for the chosen default; the existing test passes unmodified.

source.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.

options.label: Options-object parameter for future extension
options.tradeoff: Introduce `render(label, { fill })` so later attributes (size, anchor, …) extend without further signature churn. Costs: a partial signature change for callers passing a second positional argument (none exist today in this repo), and it is more machinery than this one-slice delta strictly needs.
options.acceptanceExample: render('A') === '<text>A</text>' (unchanged); render('A', { fill: 'red' }) === '<text fill="red">A</text>'; the existing test passes unmodified.
